identity.title: Sanity Checking Causal Representation Learning on a Simple Real-World System

problem.claim: Evaluate causal representation learning methods on a simple real-world system with known causal factors.

gap.claim: The abstract highlights a gap between the theoretical promise of current CRL methods and their practical application, including failures on a simple benchmark.

contributions.claim: A controlled optical experiment is used as a real-world CRL benchmark with known inputs serving as ground truth.
Representative CRL methods fail to recover the underlying causal factors on the real system.
A synthetic data ablation diagnoses failure modes, and the authors publicly release code and datasets.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors position the benchmark as a simple real-world sanity check intended to help bridge CRL methodology toward practical methods.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The evaluated representative methods all fail to recover the known causal factors in the controlled optical experiment.
Most methods already fail on the synthetic ablation, despite its simple data-generating process; the authors interpret this as a reproducibility problem.
Common mixing-function assumptions are crucial for some methods' performance but do not hold in the real data.

narrative_sequence.summary: The study evaluates CRL methods on a purpose-built optical system satisfying core CRL assumptions and exposing known causal factors.
Representative methods fail to recover the system's underlying causal factors.
A synthetic replacement of the real data-generating process is used to probe algorithmic failure modes.
Failures on the synthetic case and mismatched mixing assumptions expose a theory–practice gap; code and datasets are released for further development and validation.

source_observation.claim: The paper tests methods on both a real system with ground truth and a simpler synthetic ablation, then relates failures to mixing-function assumptions.

lessons.interpretation: Pairing a grounded benchmark with a controlled simplification can separate real-world mismatch from failures that persist in simplified settings.
lessons.application: When introducing a new method, report performance on a real benchmark with known factors alongside an ablation that isolates the assumed generative structure.
lessons.exception: This pairing is unsuitable when no credible ground truth or meaningful simplification exists.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative metrics, baselines, method names, sample sizes, or detailed failure criteria.
It does not specify which methods depend on which mixing assumptions or how the synthetic equivalent is constructed.
The public-release location in S9 is omitted.
